title: Universal logic circuit for gate-controlled superconductor-based switches operating at liquid-helium temperatures
authors: Martin Berke, Lőrinc Kupás, Tosson Elalaily, Máté Sütő, Szabolcs Csonka, Péter Makk
abstract: The observation of the gate-controlled supercurrent (GCS) effect in superconducting nanostructures initiated major research efforts toward the realisation of superconducting-based computing architectures. Here we introduce a universal logic circuit that can be a promising superconducting building block of classical hybrid supercomputers. We demonstrate a functionally complete set of logic gates by realising the AND, OR, NOT and COPY gates. The general layout and scalability of our device, combined with recent experiments demonstrating fast switching and small voltage signals, make it a functional candidate in superconducting electronics. Our device enables the realization of all classical logic gates and the half-adder combinational logic circuit using at most three nanowires, each uniquely configured with two side-gate electrodes.
summary: This work demonstrates a functional universal logic circuit built from superconducting nanowires controlled by side-gate electrodes. By exploiting the Gate-Controlled Supercurrent effect, the authors successfully implemented all classical logic gates (AND, OR, NOT, etc.) using only three components. This establishes a promising, low-power building block for future hybrid superconducting supercomputers.
main_problem: The research aims to develop superconducting-based computing architectures to overcome scaling and power limitations of conventional CMOS electronics.
main_result: A universal logic circuit capable of implementing all classical logic gates (AND, OR, NOT, etc.) and combinational circuits like the half-adder was realized using only three superconducting nanowires.
method: The functionality is demonstrated by controlling the supercurrent in superconducting nanowires via an applied gate voltage, switching the device between a zero-voltage superconducting state and a finite-voltage normal state.
model_or_system: The system utilizes superconductor-semiconductor hybrid structures, specifically $	ext{NbTiN}$ superconducting nanowires patterned on Si substrates. The operation relies critically on the Gate-Controlled Supercurrent (GCS) effect.
key_observables: Switching current ($I_{sw}$), critical current ($I_c$) as a function of gate voltage ($V_{sg}$), and the resulting output voltage ($\approx 2 	ext{ V}$) corresponding to logical '1' or '0'.
important_parameters: Operation is performed at liquid helium temperatures ($4	ext{ K}$). Key electrical parameters include $I_{sw} \approx 332\ \mu	ext{A}$ and gate voltage ranges for suppression ($\approx 30	ext{ V}$ to $40	ext{ V}$).
main_assumptions: The primary limitation noted is the requirement for large gate voltages to achieve supercurrent suppression, and thermal fluctuations can cause small scattering on plateaus.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the device configuration using three nanowires; $V-I$ curves demonstrate switching capability; schematics show time-domain realizations of AND, OR, NOT, XOR, and half-adder logic gates.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the GCS effect as a superconducting switch. It then systematically demonstrates the realization of basic gates (AND, OR, NOT) using minimal components, culminating in the proof of universality for all classical logic functions and combinational circuits.
why_interesting: While focused on classical digital logic, the underlying physics—controlling quantum states (superconductivity) with external fields to achieve robust switching—is highly relevant to superconducting qubits and quantum circuit design.
